response.rationale: C1 is the only candidate that integrates the same raw CT findings into one causative diagnosis: herniation into the greater sciatic foramen with proximal ureteral dilatation, explaining the hydronephrosis and recurrent symptoms. R1 captures the ureteral obstruction but leaves the cause implicit; R2 captures the sciatic hernia but not the resulting ureteral obstruction/hydronephrosis; R3 draws on non-specific pain and chills/fever while ignoring the stronger ureteral imaging findings.

rejected.why: Relies on non-specific flank pain, chills, and fever, but the CT evidence centers on ureteral dilatation and herniation, without infection-specific urinary findings.
Correctly identifies herniation into the greater sciatic foramen but does not account for the concurrently described proximal ureteral dilatation and hydronephrosis.
